node-1.label: Pustules beneath fingernails accompanied by redness and swelling of distal interphalangeal joints in both hands

node-2.label: Treatment history: initially treated with oral cefuroxime, followed by retinoids with topical corticosteroids, and oral methotrexate with topical corticosteroids; despite therapy, pustules and joint swelling worsened

node-3.label: Physical examination revealed 5 erythematous swollen and tender distal interphalangeal joints accompanied by pustules under dystrophic fingernails in both hands

why.why: Hand radiography revealing bone erosions in the left middle and ring finger phalangeal heads is consistent with an inflammatory erosive arthropathy and strongly supports psoriatic arthritis with nail involvement. Negative bacterial culture and negative TB/hepatitis serologies reduce the likelihood of infectious/reactive mimics, while prior antibiotic failure and use of retinoids/methotrexate support an immune-mediated process. However, psoriasis history, specific nail signs, and inflammatory markers remain unretrieved, and lack of RF/anti-CCP/MRI limits certainty; confidence is raised from 0.6 to 0.7.

Negative bacterial culture and negative TB/hepatitis serologies argue against an infectious etiology, and prior cefuroxime failure makes simple bacterial infection less likely. Hand radiography showing phalangeal head erosions is more typical of inflammatory erosive arthropathy than infection, though deep/resistant osteomyelitis cannot be fully excluded without MRI; confidence is lowered from 0.2 to 0.1.

Negative bacterial culture and negative TB/hepatitis serologies argue against a reactive process triggered by these infections, and the erosive DIP pattern with nail pustules/dystrophy is more characteristic of psoriatic arthritis. Lack of a clear triggering infection and lack of RF/anti-CCP/MRI limit further differentiation, but the available evidence makes reactive or undifferentiated inflammatory arthritis less likely; confidence is lowered from 0.2 to 0.1.
